Several of the cleanest OSAT/memory-backend beneficiaries appear non-US-listed, including Powertech and Asian substrate suppliers; US-listed discovery may be stronger in tools, test interfaces, inspection/metrology and equipment than in pure OSAT capacity.

node: Advanced packaging, HBM backend, memory packaging/test, fan-out panel-level packaging, and OSAT capacity
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI advanced-packaging/HBM-backend OSAT capacity node. The strongest US-listed direct node exposure is Amkor as an OSAT reference/overflow candidate. The underfollowed discovery lane is better represented by enabling tools and capacity chokepoints: probe cards for HBM wafer test, advanced packaging process-control/metrology, and assembly equipment used in advanced packaging transitions. Non-US reference evidence from Powertech and SemiLens supports the broader bottleneck hypothesis that HBM/AI packaging can crowd out backend capacity and push value into outsourced assembly/test and adjacent equipment suppliers, but those claims require company-specific validation for US-listed candidates.
